knowledge:
- key_parameters: count=Input count matrix (dense or sparse dgCMatrix) used to initialize the scNMFSet object ;; remove.zeros=Logical indicating whether to remove empty rows and columns during initialization or filtering ;; umi.min/umi.max=Lower and upper thresholds of UMI counts for filtering cells ;; markers=A vector of pre-selected marker genes used to guide gene selection and feature mapping ;; vmr.min=Minimum variance-to-mean ratio threshold for selecting highly variable genes ;; rescue.genes=Logical indicating whether to rescue genes with modes at nonzero counts during gene filtering ;; ranks=A vector of integers specifying the factorization ranks (number of clusters) to evaluate ;; nrun=Number of independent runs with randomized initializations to avoid local maxima ;; criterion=Stopping criterion for factorization, either 'connectivity' (stable cluster membership) or 'likelihood' (stable log-likelihood) ;; Tol=Convergence tolerance threshold for stopping iterations ;; hyper.update.n0=Number of initial steps before starting hyperparameter updates in Bayesian NMF ;; unif.stop=Logical indicating whether to terminate the rank scan if a uniform column is found in the basis matrix (default TRUE)
- alternatives: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is mentioned as a traditional alternative, but NMF is preferred because it leverages the non-negative nature of count data. Generic NMF packages (e.g., NMF) and NMFEM are mentioned, but ccfindR is preferred because its Bayesian formulation provides a statistically well-controlled marginal likelihood (ML) to determine the optimal rank and construct hierarchical trees.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing single-cell RNA-seq transcript-count data (especially UMI counts from platforms like 10x Genomics) to perform quality control, identify cell types/subtypes via unsupervised clustering, determine the optimal number of clusters, and visualize cluster hierarchies.
- pitfalls: NMF optimization is sensitive to initialization and can get trapped in local maxima; users must run multiple initializations (nrun > 1) to ensure stable and reproducible results. Setting cell or gene filtering thresholds too stringently may discard biologically relevant cells or marker genes. If unif.stop is set to TRUE, the rank scan will terminate early with a warning if redundant/uniform clusters are detected.

workflows.name: maximum_likelihood_nmf
workflows.intent: Perform unsupervised clustering of single-cell RNA-seq data using Maximum Likelihood NMF and evaluate factorization quality across multiple ranks.
input: matrix.mtx (sparse UMI count matrix in MatrixMarket format)
workflows.stages: 1. Read 10x Genomics data to create an scNMFSet object ;; 2. Filter cells based on UMI count thresholds ;; 3. Filter genes based on variance-to-mean ratio (VMR) and minimum cell expression ;; 4. Perform Maximum Likelihood NMF factorization across a range of ranks ;; 5. Evaluate factorization quality measures (dispersion, cophenetic correlation) to determine rank.
workflows.code:
sc <- read_10x(dir = dir, count = 'matrix.mtx', genes = 'genes.tsv', barcodes = 'barcodes.tsv')
sc <- filter_cells(sc, umi.min = 10^2.6, umi.max = 10^3.4)
markers <- c('CD4','CD8A','CD8B','CD19','CD3G','CD3D',
             'CD3Z','CD14')
sc0 <- filter_genes(sc, markers = markers, vmr.min = 1.5, 
            min.cells.expressed = 50, rescue.genes = FALSE)
sc <- factorize(sc, ranks = seq(3,7), nrun = 5, verbose = 1, progress.bar = FALSE)
measure(sc)
plot(sc)

workflows.name: bayesian_nmf_and_hierarchy
workflows.intent: Perform unsupervised clustering of single-cell RNA-seq data using Bayesian NMF, automatically determine the optimal rank, and visualize clusters and their hierarchical relationships.
input: matrix.mtx (sparse UMI count matrix in MatrixMarket format)
workflows.stages: 1. Read 10x Genomics data to create an scNMFSet object ;; 2. Filter cells based on UMI count thresholds ;; 3. Filter genes with optional rescue of genes with modes at nonzero counts ;; 4. Perform Bayesian NMF factorization across a range of ranks ;; 5. Determine the optimal rank using marginal likelihood (evidence) ;; 6. Visualize basis (feature) and coefficient (cell) maps ;; 7. Visualize clusters using t-SNE ;; 8. Build and plot a hierarchical tree of clusters across ranks.
workflows.code:
sc <- read_10x(dir = dir, count = 'matrix.mtx', genes = 'genes.tsv', barcodes = 'barcodes.tsv')
sc <- filter_cells(sc, umi.min = 10^2.6, umi.max = 10^3.4)
markers <- c('CD4','CD8A','CD8B','CD19','CD3G','CD3D',
             'CD3Z','CD14')
sc_rescue <- filter_genes(sc, markers = markers, vmr.min = 1.5, min.cells.expressed = 50,
                          rescue.genes = TRUE, progress.bar = FALSE)
rownames(sc_rescue) <- rowData(sc_rescue)[,2]
sb <- sc_rescue
sb <- vb_factorize(sb, ranks = seq(2,7), nrun = 5, verbose = 1, Tol = 1e-4, progress.bar = FALSE)
measure(sb)
plot(sb)
optimal_rank(sb)
feature_map(sb, markers = markers, rank = 5, max.per.cluster = 4, gene.name = rowData(sb)[,2],
         cexRow = 0.7)
cell_type <- c('B_cell','CD8+_T','CD4+_T','Monocytes','NK')
colnames(basis(sb)[ranks(sb) == 5][[1]]) <- cell_type
rownames(coeff(sb)[ranks(sb) == 5][[1]]) <- cell_type
cell_map(sb, rank = 5)
visualize_clusters(sb, rank = 5, cex = 0.7)
tree <- build_tree(sb, rmax = 5)
tree <- rename_tips(tree, rank = 5, tip.labels = cell_type)
plot_tree(tree, cex = 0.8, show.node.label = TRUE)
